entities.title: ai-agent
entities.summary: `zazzle agent llm` and `zazzle agent prompt`: runs open-weight models (Qwen, Gemma 4, gpt-oss) on the developer's own machine with llama.cpp. `llm` lists a pinned catalogue of ten GGUF models, downloads one and makes it and an effort the default, or removes one; `prompt` asks a model and streams its answer, downloading the model first when it is missing; `status` reports the model store (default, downloaded models checked by size or SHA-256, partial downloads, disk use) as text or JSON; `prune` removes every model but the default, stale partial downloads and orphaned locks.
entities.purpose: The crate of the ai-agent binary: Cargo.toml (each dependency commented with its one reason, and the `metal` feature for GPU inference on Apple Silicon), the user README, and the binary and its unit tests in src/. It is one member of the Cargo workspace in src/macos.
boundaries: It is a JIT tool: not in the release tarball, the bottle or the formula. The zazzle invoker (src/macos/zazzle) execs `zazzle daemon llm llm|prompt ..`, and daemon (src/macos/daemon/src/tools.rs) uses a ai-agent beside itself or downloads it from icelander.net, checks it against the manifest compiled into daemon and execs it.
It downloads model files itself, from huggingface.co at the commit and SHA-256 its catalogue pins, into its own directory (~/.zazzle/v1/llm by default); the daemon never sees a model.

release/tools.sh builds it (universal on macOS, with Metal for Apple Silicon) and writes the tool manifest; release.sh in the continuous_integration_and_delivery repository signs and uploads it. Workspace release builds leave it out (`--exclude ai-agent`).
